newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Spanish trawler held after fatal Irish collision.
newsitem.headline: Spanish trawler held after fatal Irish collision.

text.p: An English-registered Spanish trawler was detained on Monday after a collision off the Irish coast in which the captain of an Irish fishing boat was killed, police said.
The trawler Sea Horse was being held "for examination" after a court in Bantry, County Cork, granted a police application for a 48-hour detention order, a police spokesman said.
Police said no one had been arrested, but the trawler crew would probably be interviewed on Tuesday by officials of the Irish Department of the Marine.

The Irish boat sank after the collision off the southern tip of Ireland on Sunday.The Spanish vessel picked up three of its crew, but one, the captain, was dead on arrival at hospital in Cork, police said.

"An Irish fishing vessel, the Exodus, was in a collision with the English-registered Sea Horse which is manned by a Spanish crew," said a coastguard spokesman. "The circumstances are still vague. The weather was reasonable and there was good visibility."
